parts.summary: The FCC comments argue that the E-Rate program should adapt to the ubiquitous availability of broadband to remain relevant and cost-efficient. The comments oppose limiting or sunsetting E-Rate, as the program funds should not be used to overbuild existing commercial networks providing similar services. The comments also argue that E-Rate should not be limited to areas served by a single provider, as broadband is currently available from multiple providers in almost every community.
